sections.h2: Where is Boulder and how did it start?
sections.html:
Boulder is a home rule city and the seat of Boulder County, at the base of the Rocky Mountain foothills about 25 miles northwest of Denver. The city covers about 27.4 square miles, and the 40th parallel runs along Baseline Road.

Prospectors led by Thomas Aikins reached Boulder Canyon in late 1858, and gold turned up along Boulder Creek in early 1859. The city incorporated on November 4, 1871. The University of Colorado was authorized in 1861 and opened in 1877.

The 2020 census counted 108,250 residents, and a 2024 estimate put the city at 106,803.

The university, research labs and a few large companies dominate. These are 2022 figures from the city's financial report as summarized on Wikipedia.

That mix makes Boulder a student and research town, so seller timing often follows the academic year.

sections.h2: What is Boulder's weather like for homeowners?
sections.html:
Boulder is semi-arid with many sunny days, about 21 inches of precipitation a year and 88 inches of snow in an average season. Summers bring frequent afternoon thunderstorms and about 30 days at or above 90 degrees.

The record high is 104 degrees (June 25, 2012) and the record low is minus 33 (January 17, 1930). Heavy snow load and sudden storms are the reasons buyers check roofs and drainage on foothill houses.

sections.h2: Is flood risk a factor when selling a Boulder house?
sections.html:
Yes. The city calls itself the number one flash flood risk community in Colorado, and a house in a mapped floodplain changes the insurance conversation.

  • With most policies there is a 30-day wait before flood insurance takes effect, so buyers should not wait.
  • The city joined the federal Community Rating System in 1992 and earned a Class 5 rating in early 2013, giving standard policyholders a 25% discount.
  • An elevation certificate prepared by a Colorado licensed surveyor can lower premiums, and the city lets you search for one on file.
  • New residential construction must sit at least two feet above the 100-year flood elevation.

Check the city's interactive floodplain map for your address before you list.

sections.h2: What rental rules affect a Boulder sale?
sections.html:
A rental property in Boulder needs an approved rental license before it can be used or advertised as a rental. Approval depends on inspections for health and safety, mechanical systems and energy efficiency.

The efficiency piece is SmartRegs, which requires all licensed rental housing in the city to meet a basic energy standard. The city says the approval process can take several weeks at a minimum. If a buyer plans to rent the house, they have to start this process, and the SmartRegs guide is aimed at realtors in that situation too.

sections.h2: How do roads, transit and open space work in Boulder?
sections.html:
Boulder has RTD bus service, including the Flatiron Flyer bus rapid transit route to Denver, and US 36 and state highways. The city has no rail transit, and it has an extensive network of bike paths and underpasses.

Boulder Valley School District runs most public schools, with a few northeast areas served by St. Vrain Valley. Nearly 60% of city open space, about 35,584 acres, is open to the public.

sections.h2: How are Boulder property taxes and the deed handled?
sections.html:
Boulder County bills the tax, and the state schedule applies: pay in full by April 30 or in two halves by the last day of February and June 15. For 2026 the state guide lists residential rates of 6.8% for local governments and 7.05% for schools.

The Boulder County Clerk and Recorder records the deed. The recording fee for a document was $43 effective July 1, 2025, and a transfer deed over $500 is assessed the state documentary fee of $.01 per $100. In person service is Monday through Thursday, 7:30 a.m. to 5 p.m., and there are drop boxes in Boulder, Lafayette and Longmont.

The county uses the grantee's mailing address on the deed to send the tax statements after a sale.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house in Boulder?
sections.html:
You can list it, sell it yourself, or take a cash offer. Boulder houses with flood exposure, unlicensed rental history or deferred maintenance often take longer on the open market.

A cash sale is as is, so there are no repairs to arrange. Send us your Boulder address and we will explain how a sale would work.

faqs.q: How far is Boulder from Denver?
faqs.a: About 25 miles northwest of Denver, at the foothills of the Rocky Mountains.

faqs.q: Is Boulder in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Parts of it are. Use the city's interactive floodplain map, and note that flood insurance has a 30-day waiting period.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to rent my Boulder house?
faqs.a: Yes. The city requires an approved rental license before a property can be used or advertised as a rental, and licensing includes SmartRegs energy standards.

faqs.q: What is the Boulder County recording fee?
faqs.a: The county lists $43 per document as of July 1, 2025, plus a state documentary fee of $.01 per $100 on transfer deeds over $500.

faqs.q: Who is the largest employer in Boulder?
faqs.a: The University of Colorado Boulder, with 6,200 employees in 2022 figures.
